content: 1. A document on digital health, accessed on December 16, 2020, provides insights into the advancements and strategies in the field as of September 2020. 2. The draft global strategy on digital health for 2020–2025, accessed on December 16, 2020, outlines a comprehensive plan for leveraging digital technologies to improve health outcomes globally. 3. 4. The digital strategy for 2020–2024, accessed on December 16, 2020, highlights key initiatives and frameworks for integrating digital solutions into health systems. 5. The Global Fund's strategic framework for data use at the country level (2017–2022), accessed on December 16, 2020, emphasizes actionable data-driven improvements in health systems. 6. The WHO guideline on digital interventions for health system strengthening, accessed on October 8, 2020, provides evidence-based recommendations for implementing digital health solutions. 7. A classification of digital health interventions, accessed on October 8, 2020, categorizes various digital tools and their applications in health systems. 8. Barton et al. (2011) demonstrated the collect once, use many approach by integrating public health secondary data use requirements into an existing domain analysis model. 9. Mehl et al. (2021) introduced the WHO SMART guidelines, which aim to optimize the use of guideline recommendations at the country level in the digital age. 10. Boxwala et al. (2011) proposed a multi-layered framework for disseminating knowledge through computer-based decision support systems. 11. The fifth edition of the medical eligibility criteria for contraceptive use provides updated guidance on safe and effective contraceptive methods. 12. The third edition of selected practice recommendations for contraceptive use, accessed on January 26, 2021, offers practical advice for family planning providers. 13. The WHO and Johns Hopkins University published the third edition of the Family Planning: A Global Handbook for Providers, accessed on January 26, 2021, as a comprehensive resource for family planning services. 14. The Universal Health Coverage (UHC) compendium, accessed on December 17, 2020, serves as a repository of interventions to achieve UHC goals. 15. The Collaborative Requirements Development Methodology (CRDM), accessed on February 11, 2021, provides a structured approach to developing public health informatics solutions. 16. The Handbook for Digitalizing Primary Health Care, accessed on January 26, 2021, focuses on optimizing person-centered tracking and decision-support systems across care pathways. 17. WHO and UNICEF's guidance on analyzing and using health facility data for RMNCAH program managers, accessed on April 19, 2021, offers practical recommendations for data-driven decision-making. 18. The National eHealth Strategy Toolkit, accessed on September 18, 2020, provides a framework for developing and implementing national eHealth strategies. 19. A document on classifying health workers, accessed on September 18, 2020, maps occupations to the international standard classification system. 20. WHO recommendations on antenatal care for a positive pregnancy experience, accessed on October 8, 2020, provide evidence-based guidance for improving maternal health. 21. WHO's OptimizeMNH guidelines, accessed on January 10, 2019, focus on task-shifting strategies to enhance access to maternal and newborn health interventions. 22. A document on common requirements for maternal health information systems, accessed on November 16, 2018, outlines essential components for effective data management. 23. The Digital Adaptation Kit for Family Planning provides tools for integrating digital solutions into family planning services. 24. A fact sheet on family planning and contraception methods, accessed on January 26, 2021, offers concise information on available contraceptive options. 25. The decision-making tool for family planning clients and providers, accessed on January 27, 2021, serves as a technical guide for informed contraceptive choices. 26. The WHO consolidated guideline on self-care interventions for sexual and reproductive health, accessed on March 25, 2021, emphasizes empowering individuals to manage their health. 27. The adolescent job aid, accessed on January 26, 2021, is a practical reference tool for primary-level health workers addressing adolescent health needs. 28. WHO recommendations on adolescent sexual and reproductive health, accessed on January 26, 2021, provide evidence-based guidance for improving adolescent health outcomes. 29. The clinical handbook on healthcare for women subjected to intimate partner violence or sexual violence, accessed on October 14, 2020, offers practical guidance for healthcare providers. 30. WHO's clinical and policy guidelines on responding to intimate partner violence and sexual violence against women, accessed on April 21, 2021, provide a comprehensive framework for addressing gender-based violence. 31. Guidance on contraceptive eligibility for women at high risk of HIV, accessed on May 10, 2021, offers recommendations on safe contraceptive methods for this population. 32. Barden-O’Fallon and Reynolds assessed family planning service delivery indicators across implementing partners, highlighting key metrics for evaluation. 33. The Family Planning 2020 core indicators, accessed on May 10, 2021, provide standardized metrics for monitoring progress in family planning initiatives. 34. The second edition of the WHO's technical and policy guidance on safe abortion offers updated recommendations for health systems. 35. Programming strategies for postpartum family planning, accessed on May 10, 2021, provide actionable guidance for integrating family planning into postpartum care. 36. A consensus definition of digital health, presented in 2019, outlines key terms and the theory of change for digital health and interoperability. 37. A practical guide for developing health management information systems in developing countries, accessed on October 8, 2020, offers step-by-step recommendations for implementation. 38. The International Classification of Diseases (ICD) information sheet, accessed on October 8, 2020, provides an overview of the global standard for disease classification. 39. HL7 FHIR Release 4, accessed on June 17, 2021, details data types and standards for health information exchange.
